name: MUNCH
description: A tall museum on the harbour front devoted to Edvard Munch, with thousands of his paintings, prints and drawings.

name: Fram Museum
description: A museum on the Bygdøy peninsula built around the polar ship Fram, which you can go aboard, and the history of polar exploration.

name: Kon-Tiki Museum
description: A museum on Bygdøy holding the balsa raft Kon-Tiki, sailed across the Pacific in 1947, and other boats from Thor Heyerdahl’s voyages.

name: Oslo City Hall
description: The brick city hall with two towers on the harbour, where the Nobel Peace Prize is presented each December. The halls are covered in murals.

name: Royal Palace
description: The king’s official residence, at the top of Karl Johans gate, in a public park, with a daily changing of the guard.

name: Helvete record shop (former)
places: Former Helvete record shop, Schweigaards gate
description: A former record shop near the central station that was the meeting place of Norway’s early-1990s black metal scene.

name: Museum of the Viking Age
places: Museum of the Viking Age (Viking Ship Museum)
description: The museum on Bygdøy built for three Viking ships found in burial mounds, being rebuilt and enlarged as the Museum of the Viking Age.

name: National Museum
description: Norway’s largest art museum, opened in 2022 by the harbour, with art and design from ancient times to today, including Munch’s The Scream.

name: Akershus Fortress
description: A medieval castle and fortress on the harbour, later a royal residence, with ramparts you can walk and a museum of the wartime resistance.
